prompt:
You run weekly onboarding A/B tests. Here is every finished test so far: what you predicted
and what was measured.

- round 1: Interactive Pet Customization Stage [adoption, redesign]: predicted +12.0%, measured +3.7% (p=0.294632), lost: no clear effect
- round 1: Defer Sign-In After Pet Selection [sign_in, reorder]: predicted +10.0%, measured +0.3% (p=0.907176), lost: no clear effect
- round 1: Pet Generation Waiting Screen Tips & Timer [home, wait_info]: predicted +8.0%, measured +8.9% (p=0.000775), won
- round 2: Desktop Controls Quick Reference Screen [finish, new_screen]: predicted +6.0%, measured -2.6% (p=0.58592), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Photo Upload Quality Guidance Flow [adoption, new_flow]: predicted +4.0%, measured +5.9% (p=0.12023), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Explicit Account Pet Sync Copy [sign_in, copy]: predicted +5.0%, measured -3.4% (p=0.197813), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Desktop Pet Display & Launch Status Indicator [home, wait_info]: predicted +8.0%, measured -3.5% (p=0.216343), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Fast Track Path Choice Guidance [choose_path, hint]: predicted +5.0%, measured -2.5% (p=0.23735), lost: no clear effect

Previous lessons:
Adding tips and a timer to waiting screens (wait_info) was helpful (+8.9% measured, p=0.000775), slightly exceeding the predicted +8.0%.
Redesigning the pet customization stage (redesign) showed no clear effect (+3.7%, p=0.295), falling far short of the +12.0% prediction.
Deferring sign-in after pet selection (reorder/sign_in) showed no clear effect (+0.3%, p=0.907), far below the +10.0% prediction.
Predictions for redesigns and step reordering were significantly too optimistic.

Rewrite the lessons: at most 6 short rules about which kinds of change worked, which did not, and
where your predictions were too high or too low. Call a kind of change helpful only if a test of that
kind won (was significant); for tests with no clear effect, say no effect was seen, even if the numbers
lean one way. Keep rules that still hold, drop ones the data contradicts. Return JSON {"lessons": ["..."]}

lessons: Adding tips and a timer to waiting screens was helpful (+8.9%, p=0.0008), matching predictions (+8.0%).
Redesigning onboarding stages (redesign) and reordering steps (reorder) showed no clear effect, falling far short of optimistic predictions.
Adding new screens (new_screen), new guidance flows (new_flow), or path hints (hint) showed no clear effect.
Changing copy (copy) and adding desktop status indicators showed no clear effect.
Predictions for redesigns, step reordering, copy changes, and guidance additions were consistently too high.
